page: Amazon Web Services im4gn.16xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor and powered by 64-bit Arm-based AWS Graviton2 processors (Neoverse-N1). The configuration delivers 64 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. It includes 256.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per core), 30,000 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps. No dedicated GPUs are attached.

Benchmark results highlight strong throughput across multi-threaded and I/O-heavy operations. The instance achieves strong performance in multi-core stress testing (97,045.1 in stress-ng), Clang software compilation (42,813.0), Redis SET throughput (72.61 million ops/sec), and static web serving throughput (46.08 GB/sec). Conversely, single-core execution metrics, such as Geekbench single-core (971.0) and single-threaded gzip compression (20.34 GB/sec), place in the lower quartile, reflecting the architectural emphasis on core density rather than single-thread clock frequencies.

The dense integration of 30 TB high-speed local NVMe storage combined with a 100 Gbps network interface provides high qualitative cost efficiency for data-intensive architectures. Workloads that can divide data pipelines across 64 dedicated Arm cores will maximize the return on resource density, whereas applications reliant on single-threaded IPC or x86-specific instruction sets will face performance bottlenecks.

This instance profile is best suited for high-throughput distributed databases, large-scale Redis caching layers, log indexing clusters, data lakes, and continuous integration compilation pipelines that require rapid local disk access and broad parallel compute capability.

In benchmark evaluations, it demonstrates high efficiency in parallel compute and fast I/O workloads, recording strong results in multi-core stress testing, software compilation, Redis operations (72.61 million ops/sec), and static web throughput. Single-threaded metrics, including Geekbench single-core, show weaker relative performance, confirming a core-count-oriented architecture over peak per-core speed. With its high NVMe storage capacity and dense dedicated physical cores, the im4gn.16xlarge is primarily suited for distributed databases, caching clusters, and high-volume data analytics engines.
